report.root_cause: The OPS-250 deploy of server.properties (deploy/2026-11-01-server-properties.md) was only supposed to raise max-players from 20 to 40. It also set white-list=true and enforce-whitelist=true while whitelist.json was empty ([]). After the deploy restart, every player (Steve_Mines, Alex_Builds, new players) was kicked with "You are not whitelisted on this server!".
report.actions: 1. Checked the baseline status and server.properties. 2. Saw the server go down for the deploy restart. Compared the new server.properties with deploy/previous/server.properties and read the deploy note: the whitelist changes were not intended. 3. Declared the incident. 4. While the server was still starting, rewrote server.properties with white-list=false and enforce-whitelist=false, keeping max-players=40. The server had already loaded the bad values, so this write did not take effect. 5. Tried to start the server; it was already running, so nothing happened. 6. Once it was up, confirmed whitelist rejections in the log, then ran the console command 'whitelist off'. 7. Saw that the server had rewritten server.properties with enforce-whitelist=true, so I set it back to false (white-list=false, max-players=40 kept). 8. Verified: players are joining again (Steve_Mines and Alex_Builds online, newplayerNN logins accepted), with no whitelist rejections after 06:40:38. TPS is 20. I did not restart the server.
report.residual_risk: enforce-whitelist=false in server.properties will only be loaded at the next restart; the running server just has the whitelist turned off, which makes enforcement moot. Whoever deployed should fix their source copy of server.properties so the next deploy doesn't bring the whitelist settings back. The intended max-players=40 change is kept.
